exact_statement: For every finite uniform-cube Boolean sign f with masses p_S and influences e_i, let F_J replace each physical coordinate i in J by a disjoint pair parity u_i v_i. Then H(F_J)=H(f), I(F_J)=I(f)+sum_J e_i and M(F_J)=M(f)-sum_J M_i(f), where M_i=e_i[log2(1/e_i)-D(mu_i||r_i)] with complete normalized row laws mu_i(T)=p_(T+i)/e_i,r_i(T)=p_T+p_(T+i). Each duplicated row u_i or v_i has zero M and zero erasure. Marginalizing only its partner occupancy loses exactly M_i(f) of influence-weighted KL. In contrast retaining only that partner gives laws mu=(0,1),r=(1-e_i,e_i), preserves the complete KL log2(1/e_i) and loses zero refund. Independent common spectator factors can be discarded with zero loss in this binary quotient. All-pair deletion loss divided by total physical influence equals M(f)/I(f) if J is all coordinates. For every even d>=2 an actual witness G(u,v,y)=g(uv,y), g(s,y)=b(y)-1_{y=0}+s 1_{y=0}, b(y)=(-1)^(sum_j y_(2j-1)y_(2j)), has Inf_u=Inf_v=delta=2^-d, I(G)=d/2+(d+2)delta, H(G)/I(G)<=3, and each partner-deletion loss lies in [delta(d-1),delta d]. The reference partner and core are genuinely correlated. Thus no fixed local influence allowance using only the queried/erased pair pays this loss, even though the opposite binary quotient retains it exactly. No universal terminal-core payment or FEI disproof is asserted.
hypotheses: Actual finite Boolean signs on the uniform physical cube; bits and ordinary flip influence
Disjoint two-bit parity substitutions, with no assertion of influence invariance under general linear changes
Complete reference probabilities retained, including derivative-free mass; irrelevant rows omitted
Bent witness even d>=2; y uses 0/1 labels of the uniform cube

exact_statement: For every even integer d>=2, put delta=2^-d, t=2^(-d/2), b(y)=(-1)^(sum_j y_(2j-1)y_(2j)) on 0/1 labels, q(u,v)=-1 only at (1,1), and F_d=b(y)+1_(y=0)(q(u,v)-1). Every Fourier atom of F_d is positive. Each query i in {u,v} has e_i=delta/2 and positive true erasure. Retaining only the other pair coordinate gives complete derivative/reference laws (1/2,1/2) and (1-e_i,e_i). With N_+=(2^d+2^(d/2))/2,N_-=(2^d-2^(d/2))/2 and D0=sum_sigma N_sigma delta log2[(1-delta/2)/(1-sigma t+delta/2)], the full KL equals binary KL plus D0/2 and the influence-weighted quotient loss is L_i=e_i D0/2. Uniformly 0<L_i/e_i<=log2(7/5)/2<1/4-1/256, certified by 7^128<2^63*5^128. The two losses together are <delta/4 and <Inf_(y1)/10 if that physical reserve is dedicated only to these losses. Nevertheless M_i/e_i>d/2+3/4. Each core influence equals (1+delta)/2, I(F_d)=d/2+(d/2+1)delta, and H(F_d)/I(F_d)<=2+4/d<=4. No universal conditional partition, terminal payment, or FEI conclusion is asserted.

Even d>=2, the specified quadratic bent core and two-bit gate on disjoint physical coordinates
